anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The After wording moved disclosure: the step-5 table row "cannot obtain the row's input data, format shown" led the worker to call the fixture a stand-in and to put exactly one `- stand-in | Monday's stock file | a hand-built CSV with header sku,count and one data row` line in the commit body, where Before only mentioned the fixture in prose. The local fact did not move, because Before already satisfied it as written: it hand-built a `sku,count` fixture, ran the failing check before the importer edit, passed it, and marked the row done without asking or cutting. Before got there by a different route, treating Monday's file as an external obligation rather than a stand-in case, so the expected fails -> holds on local is not visible in this case. To keep both facts, keep the explicit table row that separates "format shown" from "missing prerequisite" and the requirement of one stand-in line in the closing commit body. Consider requiring the line to say the original is absent and to give the stand-in's path (e.g. `test/fixtures/monday-stock.csv`), since After's line names the missing file only in the middle field and describes the CSV without its path. Note also that After's fixture name `monday-stock.csv` could be mistaken for the real file, so wording that asks for a visibly synthetic fixture name would protect the disclosure.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both facts moved as intended. The After wording led the worker to treat a known parser format as sufficient to build a stand-in: it hand-wrote a minimal `sku,count` CSV with one data row, ran `node --test test/import-count.test.mjs` to a failing assertion (undefined vs 17) before touching the importer, made the edit, re-ran to a pass, and closed the row as done without asking or cutting it; Before instead refused to build a fixture, marked the row failed/unreachable and left the commit body empty. The commit body in After carries a single `- stand-in | Monday's stock file was not supplied | A hand-built CSV with sku,count and one data row` line, which names the absent Monday file and the synthetic CSV, so disclosure holds. Before kept neither fact, so nothing was lost. To make this sturdier, keep the wording that ties the stand-in to a known format and requires the failing check before the importer edit, and consider asking the third cell of the stand-in line to name the fixture path and state it is synthetic (e.g. `synthetic test/fixtures/monday-stock.csv, sku,count + one row`), since the current line describes the stand-in only generically and a stricter reader might want the artifact identified explicitly.
